fieldTypeBlockSelectorCommonUse2: Block at the end of article
fieldTypeBlockSelectorDescription: The Block Selector field allows a user to select a unique variant of any block model they would like to see rendered on their page.
fieldTypeBlockSelectorProTip: These are great to use when you want to use different end blocks at the end of different pages of the same model
fieldTypeBlockSelectorShortDesc: Link to a variant of a block model
fieldTypeBlockSelectorSubHeader: Link to a variant of a block model
fieldTypeBooleanCommonUse1: To callout featured blog posts, products
fieldTypeBooleanCommonUse3: To callout Badges such as "Pro Author"
fieldTypeBooleanDescription: This field is for when you want a field to only have two possible values. E.g. yes or no, true or false, featured or not featured, etc.
fieldTypeBooleanProTip: Use boolean fields to filter out items you want to show in a collection of items.
fieldTypeBooleanSubHeader: Used to set true or false values
fieldTypeColorDescription: This field is perfect for when you want to style different elements on your page such as background colors, text colors, borders, etc. Contributors will be given a color picker to select a color of their choice.
fieldTypeColorProTip: Color pickers can be used to call out items in a unique way and allow a user to easily differentiate between items.
fieldTypeColorShortDesc: Background colors, font colors, and more
fieldTypeColorSubHeader: Used for Background colors, font colors, and more
fieldTypeCurrencyCommonUse1: Cost Price of a Product or Service
fieldTypeCurrencyCommonUse2: Selling Price of a Product or Service
fieldTypeCurrencyDescription: This field is for when you want to store a cost, price, or account balance.
fieldTypeCurrencyProTip: Use currency fields instead of number fields if you want to store prices.
fieldTypeCurrencySubHeader: Used for storing costs, prices, and balances
fieldTypeDateDescription:
This field is for when you want the input to be a past, present, or future date. You can customize whether a user can enter a day, month, or year or all 3.

      Zesty automatically tracks dates and times for date created, date published, and date modified so no additional fields need to be created for these.
fieldTypeDateProTip: If you want to add a time to your date then use the date time field.
fieldTypeDateShortDesc: Perfect for Birthdays, release dates, events, etc.
fieldTypeDateSubHeader: Use for birthdays, release dates, events, etc.
fieldTypeDateTimeDescription:
This field is for when you want the input to be a data and time. You can customize whether a user can enter a time, day, month, or year or all 4.

      Zesty automatically tracks dates and times for date created, date published, and date modified so no additional fields need to be created for these.
fieldTypeDateTimeProTip: If you want to only have a date then use the date field.
fieldTypeDateTimeShortDesc: Track dates along with specific times
fieldTypeDateTimeSubHeader: Use to track dates along with specific times
fieldTypeDropdownDescription: This field is for when you want a user to choose a value from a dropdown menu of pre-defined options written by you. You can define these values in the field settings.
fieldTypeDropdownProTip: The values you add to a dropdown field will only be available to the model the field is added into. If you need values that reusable and accessible in multiple models, create a separate model for it and then a single or multi item relationship field to it.
fieldTypeDropdownShortDesc: Select from a list of values
fieldTypeDropdownSubHeader: Used to allow a user to select from a list of values
fieldTypeExternalUrlCommonUse2: Link to Social Media Pages on Facebook, Instagram, etc.
fieldTypeExternalUrlCommonUse3: Link to 3rd party services like Eventbrite for events or Doordash for Orders
fieldTypeExternalUrlDescription: This field is great to store URLs to pages on external websites. These links can be displayed and clicked on by users.
fieldTypeExternalUrlProTip: You can also add links in rich text fields.
fieldTypeExternalUrlSubHeader: Use this field to link to an external website
fieldTypeIntegrationCommonUse2: 3rd Party Integration - Pull details from an external app
fieldTypeIntegrationCommonUse4: Import Content from another Zesty instance
fieldTypeIntegrationCommonUse5: External CMS - Display content from an external CMS
fieldTypeIntegrationDescription: This field allows users to fetch data from a JSON API, select entries and then add them to a content item. The data remains static until reselected. Ensuring controlled updates.
fieldTypeIntegrationProTip: The data is stored as a JSON object and can be accessed headlessly or with Parsley for dynamic rendering in templates.
fieldTypeIntegrationShortDesc: Fetch and store data from APIs
fieldTypeIntegrationSubHeader: Fetch and store data from APIs
fieldTypeInternalLinkDescription: Internal Link fields allow for the selection of an internal instance item from any schema. This can be useful for providing authors the ability to relate an item across an instance.
fieldTypeInternalLinkProTip: You can use External URL fields if you want to link to external websites.
fieldTypeInternalLinkShortDesc: Link to an internal content item
fieldTypeInternalLinkSubHeader: Use this field to link to an internal content item
fieldTypeMarkdownDescription: This field provides a contributor a Github Flavored Markdown editor syntax for styling and structuring content.
fieldTypeMarkdownProTip: This field works great when you want to contributors to apply any styling and structure to text.
fieldTypeMarkdownShortDesc: Light weight markup to format text
fieldTypeMarkdownSubHeader: Light weight markup to format text
fieldTypeMediaCommonUse2: Profile Pictures of Authors or Team Members
fieldTypeMediaCommonUse5: Videos of demos, tutorials, company onboarding
fieldTypeMediaCommonUse7: PDFs of whitepapers, ebooks, menus, maps, and more
fieldTypeMediaDescription: This field allows a user to add one or more media files such as an image, video, document, presentation, etc. You can set the maximum number of files a user can upload and the maximum file size for each upload.
fieldTypeMediaProTip: You can also add media in-line in rich text fields.
fieldTypeMediaShortDesc: Images, videos, PDFs, and other files
fieldTypeMediaSubHeader: Use for images, videos, PDFs, and other files
fieldTypeMultiLineTextDescription: The Multi Line Text field is best for long text content that doesn't need special formatting or have links or media.
fieldTypeMultiLineTextProTip: This field works great when you want to ensure that contributors cannot apply any styling to text.
fieldTypeMultiLineTextSubHeader: Used for descriptions, summaries, and blurbs
fieldTypeNumberDescription: This field is for when you want the input to be a number.
fieldTypeNumberProTip: Number fields can hold both whole numbers and decimals.
fieldTypeNumberSubHeader: Used for quantity, age, ratings, etc.
fieldTypeOneToManyCommonUse1: To link an Article to Multiple Authors, Tags, or Categories
fieldTypeOneToManyCommonUse2: To link an Author to Multiple Services
fieldTypeOneToManyDescription: This field allows you to connect your model to another model and connect to multiple items instead of one.
fieldTypeOneToManyProTip: It's great to use this field when you find yourself or your team repeatedly typing in the same set of inputs such as author names. For example, it makes sense to create a model of Authors and connect to it since you will else have to else repeatedly type it in for each article.
fieldTypeOneToManyShortDesc: Link to multiple content items of a model
fieldTypeOneToManySubHeader: Use this field to link to multiple content items of a model
fieldTypeOneToOneCommonUse1: To link an Article to a single Author or Category
fieldTypeOneToOneCommonUse2: To link an Employee to a single service
fieldTypeOneToOneDescription: This field is perfect for connecting your model to another model. For example, linking a blog to a category or an author.
fieldTypeOneToOneProTip: It's great to use this field when you find yourself or your team repeatedly typing in the same set of inputs such as author names. For example, it makes sense to create a model of Authors and connect to it since you will else have to else repeatedly type it in for each article.
fieldTypeOneToOneShortDesc: Link to one content item of a model
fieldTypeOneToOneSubHeader: Use this field to link to one content item of a model
fieldTypeRepeaterDescription: The Repeater Field allows you to create a group of fields for repeating content. Useful for multiple items, such as slides, team members, or FAQs.
fieldTypeRepeaterProTip: Use a Repeater Field to manage lists or sections with a shared structure but unique content like recipes or testimonials.
fieldTypeRepeaterShortDesc: A repeating list of grouped fields
fieldTypeRepeaterSubHeader: Used for groups of static fields
fieldTypeSingleLineTextDescription: The "Single Line Text" Field is best for short text content that doesn't need special formatting or have links or media.
fieldTypeSingleLineTextProTip: This field works great when you want to ensure that contributors cannot apply any styling to text.
fieldTypeSingleLineTextSubHeader: Used for Titles, names, and headings
fieldTypeSortOrderCommonUse1: Set the order of featured products
fieldTypeSortOrderCommonUse3: Set the order of videos of a course
fieldTypeSortOrderDescription: There may be times when you want to sort data, not by name or date, but by a user-defined custom order. In such a scenario, you can add a sort order field which allows you to specify the order number of each content item.
fieldTypeSortOrderProTip: You can change the default sort number with the plus and minus buttons in the content item view, as well as in the table view.
fieldTypeSortOrderSubHeader: Use to add order to content items
fieldTypeUuidDescription: The UUID field creates a unique alpha numeric string when an item is created. This is a helpful feature for analytics tracking, inventory management, user management, etc.
fieldTypeUuidProTip: UUID are always unique and are non editable.
fieldTypeUuidSubHeader: Use to set unique ids to each content item
fieldTypeWysiwygDescription: This field is best for long text content that has multiple headings, paragraphs, and in-line media such as videos, images, or links. You can also apply advanced text formatting such as bold, italics, and underline.
fieldTypeWysiwygProTip: This field works great when you want to contributors to apply any styling and structure to text.
fieldTypeWysiwygShortDesc: Long text content with links & images such as blogs
fieldTypeWysiwygSubHeader: Long text content with links & images such as blogs

Note: This change can be reverted later from General Settings

hybridDescription: Hybrid is best of both worlds. Pages still render HTML at their routes, but they can also render JSON with a simple get parameter.
hybridModeDescription:
Hybrid is best of both worlds. Pages still render HTML at their routes, but they can also render JSON with a simple get parameter. For example /about/ would return HTML, but /about/?toJSON would return a fully hydrated JSON object of the about page.

Note: This change can be reverted later from General Settings
